scenes.name: the van, the courier, and a server
scenes.visual: Frame 1920 x 1080; keep x < 420, y < 110 clear for the chapter label. A calm stage with no computers until b4. Lower-middle band, y 640 to 780: a road drawn left to right from x 300 to x 1640, with an upper lane (courier) and a lower lane (van). Left end: a post-office icon (a small building with a mailbox). Right end: three small house icons, a small person icon at the middle one's door. Neither end carries a text label; the icons say it. Letters are small blue envelope icons. Top band, y 150 to 330: two definition cards side by side (left x 480 to 900, right x 1020 to 1440) with neutral white outlines, because this scene is about neither compute nor bytes. Left card: stopwatch icon, title 'Latency'. Right card: stacked-envelopes icon, title 'Throughput', with a thin empty bar under the title that only fills in b4. Each card shows one short line only while it is being defined ('time for one letter', 'letters per day'), then keeps its title and icon alone. Each vehicle gets a one-line ledger at the right end of its lane, white, 28 px. A grey 'illustrative' tag sits bottom-right from b2 until 'Nothing here needed a computer' in b4, hidden while the b3 inset shows. In b4 one continuous morph re-dresses the same stage for a server, and only then does a slider draw on, centred under the road at y 860, labelled 'wait before sending', with a single-pill icon at its left end and a tray icon at its right end; it stays to the end of the scene. The knob makes one sweep per spoken phrase, never two in one phrase. Never more than five text items on screen besides numbers. The idea the motion makes visible: one service, two different questions, and a single dial that trades one for the other.

beats.say: What about the person waiting? Take the mail: latency, how long one letter takes; throughput, how many arrive per day.
beats.show: On 'the person waiting', a small person icon fades in at x 1500, y 700, beside an empty mailbox, with a tiny grey clock ticking above it. On 'Take the mail', the road draws on from left to right toward the person, the post office pops in at the left end and three house icons at the right end, the person settling at the middle house's door. On 'latency', the left card drops into the top band with its line 'time for one letter'; one blue envelope travels from the post office to the person's house while the card's stopwatch runs, stopping as the envelope lands and the tiny clock vanishes. On 'throughput', the right card drops in with 'letters per day'; a steady stream of envelopes flows along the road to all three houses and a counter on the card ticks upward. As the beat ends both description lines fade, leaving titles and icons.

beats.say: A van filling all week has enormous throughput and terrible latency. A courier, off with each letter, is the reverse.
beats.show: The stream stops. On 'A van', a van icon parks on the lower lane at the post office with a small grey tag 'once a week' above it; on 'filling all week', envelopes pour in and a counter on its side runs to '7,000'. On 'enormous throughput', the 'once a week' tag fades, the van drives to the houses and its ledger lands at the lane's right end: '≈ 1,000/day · up to a week'. On 'terrible latency', one envelope drops into the empty post office and waits, glowing, while a ring of seven segments around it fills one segment per day. On 'A courier', a motorbike icon on the upper lane carries one envelope to the houses in about a second; on 'off with each letter', it returns, picks up the next single envelope and repeats; its ledger lands: '≈ 20/day · under an hour'. The grey 'illustrative' tag fades in bottom-right.

beats.say: Neither is better. Unlike memory's latency and bandwidth, these often pull against each other.
beats.show: On 'Neither is better', a balance-scale icon between the two ledgers settles level, a grey tag 'different questions' beneath it. On 'Unlike memory's latency and bandwidth', that tag, both ledgers and the 'illustrative' tag fade out, and a small grey inset fades in centred just above the road (x 760 to 1160, y 420 to 600), clear of both cards: the container ship and motorbike courier from the earlier memory chapter, side by side, tagged 'independent'. Visible text is now only 'Latency', 'Throughput' and 'independent'. On 'pull against each other', the inset fades out, the ledgers and the 'illustrative' tag return, and a thin double-headed arrow draws between the 'Latency' and 'Throughput' cards and pulls taut, the two cards leaning slightly toward each other.

beats.say: Nothing here needed a computer, yet a serving system faces this choice: wait to gather requests and do more, or answer at once and do less.
beats.show: On 'Nothing here needed a computer', the 'illustrative' tag, the balance scale and both ledgers fade. On 'a serving system', one continuous morph: the post office becomes a G P U package icon, the houses and the person a row of ten user icons, the envelopes blue request pills, the van a tray on the lower lane and the motorbike a single pill on the upper lane; the cards and the double-headed arrow stay. On 'this choice', the slider draws on under the road with its label 'wait before sending', knob centred. On 'wait to gather requests', the knob slides right once: ten pills collect in the tray and leave together, the bar on the Throughput card fills, and a counter at the lower lane's right end runs to '≈ 240 tokens/s in total', with a grey sub-line beneath it, 'each user ≈ 24/s'. On 'answer at once', the knob slides left once: the tray empties, pills leave one by one on the upper lane, the Throughput bar shrinks to a tenth, and the upper lane's counter reads '≈ 24 tokens/s'; on 'do less' that counter pulses once. A small grey tag under the counters: 'H100, weights only'. Text besides numbers: 'Latency', 'Throughput', 'wait before sending', the sub-line and 'H100, weights only'.

beats.say: But the first request waits for the rest. Soon, only tokens arriving in time will count.
beats.show: On 'the first request', the knob slides right again; the leftmost pill in the tray pulses and a small stopwatch beside it runs while the other nine trickle in one by one, and the Latency card's stopwatch hand lengthens in step. On 'arriving in time', a small teal clock badge flickers once over each user icon, then fades: a promise of the chapter's last number. Final hold: the two cards in the top band, the slider, the G P U and the users.

scenes.name: two waits, and the phase behind each
scenes.visual: Keep x < 420, y < 110 clear. Opening layout: top half, a wide chat window centred (x 480 to 1440, y 130 to 420), its prompt bubble already sent and an empty reply area with a blinking cursor. Centre band, y 540: a horizontal time axis from x 240 to x 1700, schematic, with a small 'send' marker at its left end. On it, the shape of every streamed answer: an outlined pause bar from 'send' to the first token, then nine evenly spaced blue token pills. The pause bar fills amber, because it turns out to be arithmetic; the gaps between pills are marked coral, because they turn out to be bytes. From b2 the chat window fades, the timeline rises into the top band (y 200), and its labels stay at 28 px. The lower half then splits into two phase panels: left, amber outline, titled 'prefill' in b2, an 80-layer stack of thin horizontal bars with a block of blue prompt pills beneath; right, coral outline, titled 'decode' in b3, an identical stack with a single blue pill beneath. In b4 the panels shrink into two dots on a small roofline at bottom-centre, drawn as in the roofline chapter: both axes logarithmic, coral slanted ceiling, amber flat ceiling, white dashed ridge labelled '295'. At most five text items besides numbers at any moment; each beat says what leaves. The idea: one stream, two waits, and each wait made by one phase.

beats.say: Press send, and you feel two waits. The pause before the first word: time to first token. Each gap after it: time per output token.
beats.show: On 'Press send', a send-arrow icon flashes in the chat window and the 'send' marker drops onto the axis. On 'two waits', the outlined pause bar grows rightward from the marker while the cursor blinks, captioned 'a pause'. On 'the first word', the bar stops, the first blue pill lands, the reply shows 'The', and the 'send' label fades, its tick staying. On 'time to first token', the bar fills amber from left to right, 'a pause' fades, and an amber bracket draws under it labelled 'time to first token' with 'TTFT' beneath. On 'Each gap after it', eight more pills land at even spacing, each adding a word to the reply, and a coral bracket snaps into the first gap and hops once to the next, the same width. On 'time per output token', the coral bracket gains its label 'time per output token' with 'TPOT, or inter-token latency' beneath. Text at the end: the reply, the two bracket names and their two short forms.

beats.say: Prefill makes the pause: the whole prompt passes through every layer before any output. Half a second for a short prompt, several seconds for a long one. Real chips run below full speed; queues add more.
beats.show: On 'Prefill makes the pause', the chat window fades, the timeline rises into the top band, and the long names shrink away, so the brackets keep only 'TTFT' and 'TPOT'. A connector draws from the TTFT bracket down to the left panel and its title 'prefill' lands. On 'the whole prompt passes through every layer', the block of prompt pills rises into the 80-layer stack all together, the layers lighting amber from bottom to top; on 'before any output', the block leaves the top of the stack and the first pill in the top band glows. On 'Half a second', the prompt block is short and a tag '≈ 0.5 s, typical' pins to the pause bar; on 'several seconds', the block lengthens, the pause bar stretches with it and the tag changes to 'several seconds, typical'. On 'Real chips run below full speed', that tag fades and a dashed amber tick appears partway along the pause bar, labelled 'full speed', the bar beyond it turning a paler amber: the arithmetic alone would end at the tick. On 'queues add more', a short grey segment labelled 'queue' slides in at the start of the bar and pushes the rest right.

beats.say: Decode makes each gap: every token needs its own complete forward pass.
beats.show: On 'Decode makes each gap', the 'full speed' and 'queue' labels fade while the bar keeps its shading, a connector draws from the TPOT bracket to the right panel, its title 'decode' lands, and '≈ 42 ms on H100' appears at the TPOT bracket's end. On 'its own complete forward pass', a single pill climbs the whole stack, the layers lighting coral; as it exits, the next pill lands in the top band and another single pill starts its climb, twice more, in step with the gaps.

beats.say: The pause decides whether a product feels responsive; the gaps, whether text reads comfortably or stutters, breaking concentration. Both are felt, made at opposite ends of the roofline.
beats.show: The panel titles and '≈ 42 ms on H100' fade while the stacks keep their colours. On 'feels responsive', a short verdict 'feels responsive?' appears under TTFT; on 'reads comfortably', 'reads comfortably?' appears under TPOT. On 'stutters', the top-band pills jitter to uneven spacing; on 'breaking concentration', they settle back to even spacing. On 'Both are felt', the two verdicts fade. On 'opposite ends of the roofline', the two panels shrink into dots and fly onto the small roofline as it fades in at bottom-centre: the amber dot, labelled 'prefill', lands right of the dashed '295' ridge on the flat ceiling; the coral dot, labelled 'decode', lands far left on the slanted ceiling. Final hold text, white, under the roofline: 'opposite resource profiles'.

scenes.name: what a cache hit saves, and what it does not
scenes.visual: Keep x < 420, y < 110 clear. Two time lanes stacked across the centre, sharing one millisecond axis beneath them: 0 to 500 ms, drawn to scale at 3 px per ms (x 210 to 1710), ticks every 100 ms. Lane labels at the left, 28 px: top 'cold' beside a grey dashed empty-cache outline, bottom 'warm' beside a small teal cache badge. The cloud-and-sun icon with its label 'the weather conversation', exactly as in the previous chapter (ch16_s01), sits top-centre during b1 only. Each lane first shows its prompt as a strip of 1,032 hairline cells spanning the axis, then collapses into a prefill block starting at 0, after which blue token pills land one every 42 ms (126 px apart). Top band, right half, built during the scene: a two-row verdict, 'Prefill: skipped for matched tokens' with a teal tick (b1) and 'Decode: identical, still reads all 140 GB' in coral (b3); in b4 the rows condense and gain the two waits. A small grey tag bottom-right throughout: 'idealised: H100 at full speed, no network or queue'. Colours as in the previous chapter: teal = keys and values already held, amber = prefill arithmetic, coral = bytes, blue = tokens. The idea: a hit moves the first token earlier and leaves the rhythm after it untouched.

beats.say: A cache hit skips prefill for every matched token. Warm, the weather conversation prefilled five, not one thousand and thirty-two.
beats.show: The lanes, axis and lane labels draw on; the cloud-and-sun icon and its label 'the weather conversation' settle top-centre. On 'skips prefill', the top-band row 'Prefill: skipped for matched tokens' lands with its teal tick. On 'Warm', the bottom lane's strip fills teal from the left for 1,027 cells and ends in 5 amber cells; a round magnifier callout pops up over the strip's right tip, showing the 5 amber cells enlarged with '5' beside them. On 'one thousand and thirty-two', the top lane's strip fills amber across every cell, with '1,032' at its right end.

beats.say: Two hundred and six times less work, yet here only three and a half times less waiting: one read of the weights remains.
beats.show: The cloud-and-sun icon and its label, the magnifier and the strip numbers fade, and the top-band Prefill row fades out for this beat. On 'Two hundred and six times less work', both strips collapse onto the axis, to scale: the cold one into an amber block from 0 to 148 ms (442 px), the warm one into a block from 0 to 42 ms (126 px); a first blue pill lands at each block's right end, with '≈ 148 ms' above the cold one and '≈ 42 ms' above the warm one, and a one-line tag lands at the left: '206× less work'. On 'three and a half times less waiting', the tag extends to '206× less work → 3.5× less wait' and a white bracket spans the two first pills, labelled '≈ 106 ms', with a grey sub-tag beneath it: 'longer history: seconds'. On 'one read of the weights', the warm block takes a coral outline, a hairline amber sliver inside it marks its arithmetic, and the label above its pill extends to '≈ 42 ms: one 140 GB read'. Text besides numbers: 'cold', 'warm', the ratio tag, the sub-tag and the 'idealised' tag.

beats.say: Decode is untouched: every token still reads all one hundred and forty gigabytes. Making a token never depended on how the context was assembled.
beats.show: The ratio tag, the bracket and its sub-tag fade, the warm block's label shortens to '≈ 42 ms', and the Prefill row returns. On 'Decode is untouched', blue pills land in both lanes one every 42 ms, 126 px apart, and a coral bracket of identical width marks one gap in each lane, each '≈ 42 ms'. The top-band row 'Decode: identical, still reads all 140 GB' lands in coral. On 'how the context was assembled', a slim bar slides out beside each lane label: the cold one freshly made, with an amber edge; the warm one teal with a 5-cell amber tip. Both morph into the same teal bar, labelled '1,032 tokens of keys and values'; the label fades after a second.

beats.say: So caching is purely a prefill optimisation. Of the two waits you feel, it shortens only the first.
beats.show: On 'purely a prefill optimisation', the 'Prefill' row in the top band glows teal and both rows condense to their first words. On 'two waits you feel', amber brackets mark the pause in each lane, clearly different widths, and coral brackets mark one gap in each lane, exactly the same width. On 'only the first', the Prefill row becomes 'Prefill skipped → TTFT shorter' with a teal down-arrow and the amber brackets pulse once, while the Decode row becomes 'Decode identical → TPOT unchanged' and the coral brackets stay still. The brackets carry no text of their own; their colours tie them to the rows.

beats.say: Caching is often said to make the model faster. It makes it start sooner, then stream at the same speed.
beats.show: On 'make the model faster', the lanes dim to 30% and, centre, white, 'makes the model faster' appears and is struck through in grey. On 'start sooner', teal 'makes it start sooner' appears beneath. On 'the same speed', the phrases fade, the lanes brighten, and the warm lane's pills slide right until its first pill sits directly under the cold lane's first pill; every following pill lines up exactly, gap for gap. Hold.

scenes.name: two levers, and why the phases split
scenes.visual: Keep x < 420, y < 110 clear. Split screen across the upper two thirds. Left half, amber outline: a panel titled 'Improving TTFT' with a lever icon, one line 'compute: keep the arithmetic units fed', above a grid of small amber arithmetic-unit squares fed by a blue prompt block. Right half, coral outline: 'Improving TPOT' with a lever icon, one line 'bandwidth: move fewer bytes per token', above a coral pipe carrying byte particles. Each panel's line shows while it is spoken and then shrinks away, leaving the title. A gauge sits under each title and persists: amber, reading '0.29 s', with a grey sub-label '2,000-token prompt, at full speed' and, from b1 until 'Swap the H one hundred' in b2, a grey 26 px derivation '290 trillion ops ÷ 989 trillion/s'; coral, reading '42 ms'. Lower third, y 780 to 1000: one shared strip reused per beat, a chip card in b2 and three streaming lanes in b3. In b4 the two panels themselves pull apart and become two groups of machines. The idea: two waits with two different bottlenecks, so one change can move one gauge and leave the other alone, or even push it the wrong way, until the two phases get separate hardware.

beats.say: Different bottlenecks, different engineering. For a long prompt, time to first token is a compute problem: keep the arithmetic units fed.
beats.show: On 'Different bottlenecks', the two panels slide in from the left and right edges, titles only, and both gauges light. On 'a long prompt', a long blue prompt block flows into the left panel's grid and every amber square lights. On 'compute problem', the line 'compute: keep the arithmetic units fed' lands under the left title; on 'fed', a few squares flicker dark and are refilled at once by incoming work particles.

beats.say: Time per output token is a bandwidth problem: move fewer bytes per token. Swap the H one hundred for an H two hundred: same arithmetic, faster memory. The gaps shrink to our thirty milliseconds; the pause barely moves.
beats.show: The left line shrinks away. On 'bandwidth problem', the right line 'bandwidth: move fewer bytes per token' lands and byte particles flow along the coral pipe; on 'fewer bytes', the particles shrink to half size. On 'Swap the H one hundred', the right line and the derivation shrink away and a chip card slides into the lower strip: 'H100', with two rows, amber '989 trillion ops/s' and coral '3.35 TB/s'. On 'H two hundred', the card flips and its name becomes 'H200'. On 'same arithmetic', the amber row holds unchanged and a grey note 'same arithmetic' appears beside the amber gauge. On 'faster memory', the coral row counts up to '4.8 TB/s' and glows coral. On 'the gaps shrink', the coral gauge swings from '42 ms' to '29 ms' with a teal tick; on 'our thirty milliseconds', the '29 ms' pulses once. On 'the pause barely moves', the amber gauge holds at '0.29 s', its needle twitching but not moving. Text besides numbers: the two panel titles, 'H200', 'same arithmetic' and the amber sub-label.

beats.say: A change can even hurt the other. Prefill each new prompt on arrival, for a quicker first word, and streaming answers can stall.
beats.show: The chip card and the 'same arithmetic' note leave, and the coral gauge resets to '42 ms', the H100 again. The lower strip becomes three thin lanes, each led by a small user icon, with blue pills landing every 42 ms. On 'new prompt', a fourth user icon appears at the right with a long blue prompt block; on 'on arrival', an amber block 'prefill ≈ 0.29 s' drops down across all three lanes, with a small grey tag beside it, 'simplest scheduler'. On 'quicker first word', the fourth user's first pill lands as the block ends and the amber gauge glows briefly. On 'can stall', every lane's pills stop at the block; when it ends, one more 42 ms step runs and the next pill lands, and the top lane's gap is bracketed '≈ 335 ms, 8× the usual gap'. The coral gauge kicks to '335 ms' and falls back to '42 ms' as the pills resume their rhythm.

beats.say: That is why serving systems eventually split the two phases onto different hardware.
beats.show: The lanes clear. On 'serving systems', the two panels pull apart toward the left and right edges. On 'split the two phases', each morphs into a group of server-rack icons, amber 'prefill machines' on the left and coral 'decode machines' on the right, each still carrying its gauge. On 'different hardware', a teal block labelled 'keys and values' travels along an arrow between the groups, tagged 'KV transfer', and a small grey inset of the six-stop route from earlier flashes with its 'KV transfer' stop highlighted, then fades.

scenes.name: throughput against goodput
scenes.visual: Keep x < 420, y < 110 clear. Far left, at mid-height, a G P U package icon emits blue token particles along a pipe running right. Top band: a long blue bar labelled 'Throughput · all tokens per second' with a counter at its right end. Below it, a dashed grey outline of the same length labelled 'Goodput · only the ones in time', which fills teal only with tokens that arrive in time. On the pipe at centre-left, a gate drawn as a narrow doorway with a stopwatch icon above it: tokens that pass in time turn teal and rise into the goodput bar; late ones turn grey and drop into a bin below the gate, which gains its label 'missed target' in b2. Top-right from b1: a one-line targets card, 'first token ≤ 1 s · next ≤ 50 ms', with a grey 'illustrative' tag. Bottom band from b2: a crowd of small user icons, each with a little screen. The idea: goodput is not a second machine, it is a filter on the first one's output.

beats.say: Throughput is every token generated per second. Goodput filters it down to tokens delivered inside the promised latency targets, judged per request: averages hide rare delays.
beats.show: As the beat opens, the G P U appears and blue particles stream along the pipe. On 'Throughput', the blue bar draws on with its label and its counter starts running. On 'Goodput filters it', the dashed outline draws on beneath with its label and the gate drops onto the pipe; most particles pass, turn teal and fill the goodput bar, a few turn grey and fall into the still unlabelled bin. On 'promised latency targets', the targets card slides in top-right with its 'illustrative' tag, and the gate's stopwatch shows the same two marks. On 'judged per request', the stream separates into short trains of particles, one train per request with a small gap between trains, and the gate checks each train as a whole: one slow train among many quick ones turns entirely grey and drops into the bin. On 'averages hide', a grey label 'average' with a thin bracket spanning all the trains appears above the pipe, its smooth span giving no sign of the slow train; on 'rare delays', the slow train glows once in the bin, and 'average' is struck through and fades with its bracket. Text besides numbers at that moment: the two bar labels, the targets card, its 'illustrative' tag and 'average'.

beats.say: Pack thousands of requests into huge, slow batches: the counter looks impressive. But if every user stares at a blank screen for forty seconds, every token missed its target. Goodput is zero.
beats.show: On 'Pack thousands of requests', the crowd fills the bottom band and request pills from all of them pile into one enormous tray at the G P U. On 'the counter looks impressive', the stream thickens into a torrent and the throughput counter races upward, the blue bar glowing. On 'blank screen', every little screen in the crowd stays blank with a blinking cursor while a large stopwatch over the crowd runs to '40 s'; as it passes '1 s', the first-token mark on the targets card turns grey, and from then on every particle reaching the gate turns grey and drops into the bin. On 'missed its target', the bin gains its label 'missed target'. On 'Goodput is zero', the goodput bar drains to empty and its counter reads '0', while the throughput counter still races.

beats.say: Tokens nobody was willing to wait for. Goodput is throughput times the share that arrived in time.
beats.show: On 'nobody was willing to wait for', the camera pushes gently in on the overflowing grey bin, with the glowing throughput bar and the empty goodput outline side by side above it. On 'Goodput is throughput times', the camera eases back, the crowd, stopwatch, torrent and targets card clear, and an equation builds under the bars term by term: '1,000 tokens/s' as the throughput counter settles there; '× 70% in time' on 'the share'; '= 700 tokens/s' on 'arrived in time', as the goodput bar fills teal to 70% of its outline. A grey 'illustrative' tag sits beside the equation, and 300 grey tokens stack in the bin.

beats.say: Goodput, not raw throughput, is what production systems optimise. For anyone who operates a system rather than benchmarks one, no distinction matters more.
beats.show: The equation fades. On 'Goodput, not raw throughput', the word 'Goodput' enlarges and moves to centre in teal while 'Throughput' shrinks to grey above it. On 'operates a system', a small user-crowd icon appears beside 'Goodput'; on 'benchmarks one', a stopwatch-on-a-test-bench icon appears beside 'Throughput', greyed. Hold.

checks.claim: Van illustration (illustrative numbers, not from the atlas): 7,000 letters a week = 1,000 a day; the courier's 20 a day is a stated illustration

One request alone on an H100: 3.35 TB/s / 140 GB = 23.9, '≈ 24 tokens/s'; ten requests sharing one read make 239 in total, '≈ 240 tokens/s in total', each user still at 23.9, the sub-line 'each user ≈ 24/s' (weights only, matches ch12's 'each still at twenty-four'). The cost of batching here is the gathering wait (b5), not a slower stream

TPOT for one request: 140 GB / 3.35 TB/s = 41.8 ms on an H100, '≈ 42 ms'; 140 GB / 4.8 TB/s = 29.2 ms on an H200, '29 ms' on the gauge and spoken as 'our thirty milliseconds', the film's thirty milliseconds (CHAPTER_NOTES: 'the 30 ms' = 29.2 ms on an H200)

TTFT gauge for a 2,000-token prompt: about 290 trillion ops (ch12) at the H100's 989 trillion ops/s = 0.29 s at full speed, sub-labelled '2,000-token prompt, at full speed'. It is shorter than the atlas's typical 'half a second for a short prompt' (tagged '≈ 0.5 s, typical') because real chips run below full speed and requests queue; s02.b2 says so aloud ('Real chips run below full speed; queues add more')

Ridge on the H100 = 989 / 3.35 = 295 ops per byte (the dashed ridge on the small roofline); a prefill longer than about 295 tokens is compute bound, hence 'For a long prompt'. A 5-token warm prefill is 5 ops per byte, far below the ridge, so it waits on bytes

Example A, per CHAPTER_NOTES: 1,027 of 1,032 tokens held warm (a 99.5% hit), 5 prefilled; cold prefills all 1,032, 1,032 / 5 = 206 times the work. CORRECTION kept from ch15/ch16: atlas figs 44 and 47 say '906 of 911'; the film uses 1,027 of 1,032 so warm and cold describe the same conversation

Cold prefill of the 1,032-token weather conversation: 1,032 x 140 billion = 144.48 trillion ops plus 1.40 trillion of causal attention = 145.9 trillion; at 989 trillion ops/s = 147.5 ms, '≈ 148 ms' on screen (not narrated)

Warm prefill of 5 tokens: 0.7 trillion ops = 0.7 ms of arithmetic (the hairline amber sliver), but one read of 140 GB of weights = 41.8 ms plus 1,032 x 327,680 bytes of cache = 0.1 ms; total 41.9 ms, '≈ 42 ms: one 140 GB read'

206 times less prefill work gives here only 3.5 times less waiting (147.5 ms / 41.9 ms), said 'yet here only three and a half times'; the ratio holds for this short, idealised H100 case only, hence 'here' and the grey sub-tag 'longer history: seconds' (next check). CORRECTION (reviewer): the first word comes 105.6 ms sooner, which rounds to '≈ 106 ms', not the earlier draft's truncated '≈ 105 ms'; it also matches the screen's own 148 - 42

Sub-tag 'longer history: seconds': a 20,000-token history prefilled cold at full speed on an H100 is 20,000 x 140 billion + causal attention (2,621,440 ops per token pair = 4 x 80 layers x 8,192) = 3.36 s, against about 44 ms warm, so the first word comes about 3.3 s sooner
Decode step after prefill, warm or cold: the cache is the same 1,032 tokens = 0.338 GB, so each step reads 140.34 GB, 41.9 ms on an H100, '≈ 42 ms' in both lanes

H100 to H200 swap, now narrated ('Swap the H one hundred for an H two hundred: same arithmetic, faster memory'; the H one hundred is named aloud because every gap shown in s02 to s04 is its 42 ms): TPOT 41.8 to 29.2 ms; TTFT for the 2,000-token prompt stays 0.29 s because the H200's dense 16-bit arithmetic equals the H100's 989 trillion ops/s (same compute die; a hardware fact not stated in the atlas, and the one ch18.s01.b3 relies on), and the prompt's ~146 GB of bytes take only 43.6 ms on an H100 and 30.4 ms on an H200, far inside the 293 ms of arithmetic ('the pause barely moves', 'same arithmetic')

Interference (on screen, not narrated): with the simplest scheduler (grey tag 'simplest scheduler'; narration says 'can stall', since schedulers that interleave prefill with decode reduce the stall) the other streams' next token waits for the 293 ms prefill plus its own 41.8 ms decode step = 335 ms, 8.0 times the usual 41.8 ms gap, '≈ 335 ms, 8× the usual gap'. This uses ch12's upper figure of 290 trillion; the causal count of 285.2 trillion gives 330 ms, 7.9 times, so '8×' holds either way.
